To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) DBL2β from the PF11_0522 allele binds ICAM-2 in the low nanomolar range and the interaction with ICAMA-2 is not impaired by mutations in the N terminal subdomain or Loop 4, 2) full-length DBLβPF11_0222 has broad epitopes for ICAM-2 binding and 3) the N terminal sub-domain is not required for the interaction with ICMA-2.
the structure of the domain DBL2β from the malaria parasite PfEMP1 protein is related to its function and immunological recognition.

the PfEMP1 domain DBL2β from allele PF11_0522 binds to ICAM-1 with low nM affinity, and that full length DBL2β is the optimal structure for displaying functional epitope for blocking ICAM-1 binding, and that this domain has a broad surface for interaction with ICAM1 that is not significantly disrupted by individual amino-acid substitutions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure-function relationship of the DBLβ domain of a malaria parasite antigen, and the immunological properties of this antigen.
the identification of the functional and immunogenic epitopes of a malaria parasite ligand that binds to the human receptor ICAM-1.
understanding the molecular basis of the interaction between the parasite and its host.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N terminal subdomain and Loop 4 are important for the interaction of PfEMP1 DBLβ domains with ICAM- 1.

the structure-function-immunogenicity studies on the DBL2β domain of PfEMP1 PF11_0522 allele have been performed, and that this domain binds the endothelial receptor ICAM-1, but that the interaction is not impaired by the presence of the N-terminal sub-domain or Loop 4, which were previously implicated in this interaction.
the N-terminus of DBL2PF11_0522 does not contribute to the binding to ICAM-1 but is required for the induction of antibodies that block this interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DBL2betaPF11_0520 is an ICAM-1 binding domain with a broad surface of interactions that is not affected by single point mutations in the subdomains or in Loop 4.

the structure of PfEMP1 domain DBL2β from allele PF11_0520, a naturally occurring malaria variant antigen from P. falciparum, was determined at 1.9 Å resolution by X-ray crystallography and that the structure of this DBL domain is similar to the structure of the DBL2β domain of the P. falciparam 3D7 strain, a laboratory-adapted parasite strain.
the N terminal subdomain and loop 4 are not essential for binding ICAM- 1 and that the full-length DBLβ is the best antigen for inducing antibodies that block the interaction with the receptor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DBL2betaPF11_0520 is a potent ligand for ICAM1 and its interaction with this receptor is not impaired by mutations in Loop 4 or N-terminal subdomain.

the full-length PfEMP1 domain DBL2β is required to elicit antibodies that block its interaction with the ICAM-1 receptor, and that the N-terminal fragment of this domain is dispensable for this interaction.
PfEMP1 domain DBL2β is able to bind ICAM-1 through multiple epitopes and that the N terminal region is required for full binding to this endothelial receptor.
